summary: Backend ASER feature is fully working (18/19 pytest passed, 1 skipped for missing commercial creds). Frontend has a CRITICAL integration gap: the ASER entry buttons (data-testid mod-nav-aser and mod-pro-aser-open) live on MODSiteDashboard/MODProDashboard components that are imported as _MODSiteDashboard/_MODProDashboard in AppRoutes.js and never rendered. MOD site users log in and land on /pulse (regular DashboardPage / LiteDashboardPage / PulseLandingPage), which has no ASER trigger anywhere. So the entire ASER portal is currently unreachable via the UI for the target MOD user.

ui_bugs.issue: Component is imported as `_MODSiteDashboard` (unused prefix) in /app/frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.js line 199 and never rendered. The mod-nav-aser button is therefore unreachable for MOD site users who are redirected to /pulse.
Also imported as _MODProDashboard (unused) — the mod-pro-aser-open button never renders for MOD branch/org users.

integration_issues.issue: No path exists for a MOD user to open the ASER portal. AppRoutes lines 262-264 redirect all mod_site/mod_branch/mod_org users to /pulse where no ASER trigger is present. MODASERPortal is only mounted inside the two unreachable dashboards.

rca of the issue: MODSiteDashboard and MODProDashboard components exist and are complete, but AppRoutes.js imports them with underscore-prefixed names (`_MODSiteDashboard`, `_MODProDashboard`) and never places them in any <Route> or conditional render.
